newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Melbourne wins right to bid for 2006 Commonwealth Games.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Melbourne wins right to bid for 2006 Commonwealth Games.

text.p: Melbourne was named on Friday as the Australian city which will bid to host the 2006 Commonwealth Games, the Australian Commonwealth Games Association (ACGA) announced.
The Victorian capital beat Brisbane and Darwin for the right to bid for the Games.
All three cities made final submissions to the ACGA in Sydney on Friday before Melbourne was chosen.
Melbourne's main competitors for the 2006 Commonwealth Games will be Barbados, Durban and Wellington.
The winning city is to be announced in 1999.
"If we are successful we will deliver to you a professional and friendly event," Victorian Premier Jeff Kennett told reporters.
"I'm quite sure the competition was close and I trust we can rely on (Darwin and Brisbane) to help us to go on and win the bid to represent Australia," he said.
Melbourne hosted the Olympic Games in 1956.
